name: TB6612FNG Dual DC Motor Driver
max_ratings: Absolute Max VM: 15V | VCC: 6V | Output Peak: 3.2A
pin_configuration: PWMA, PWMB: PWM speed control inputs (up to 100 kHz)
AIN1, AIN2: Motor A direction logic
BIN1, BIN2: Motor B direction logic
STBY: Standby pin (Active HIGH to run motors)
key_features: High-efficiency low-RDS(on) DMOS output transistors (0.5Ω typical)
critical_warnings: STBY pin MUST be pulled HIGH (to VCC); leaving STBY floating or LOW halts all motor outputs.
Connect common GND between microcontroller and battery ground to prevent floating logic levels.

name: L298N Dual H-Bridge Motor Driver
max_ratings: Absolute Max VS: 50V | Output Peak: 3A per channel
pin_configuration: ENA, ENB: Enable pins (PWM speed control)
IN1, IN2, IN3, IN4: Direction inputs
key_features: Onboard 5V regulator jumper on standard breakout modules
critical_warnings: Darlington transistor outputs drop 1.8V to 3.2V as heat! Highly inefficient compared to MOSFET drivers like TB6612FNG.
If motor supply VS exceeds 12V, remove the 5V regulator jumper on typical breakout boards to prevent burning the onboard 78M05 regulator.

name: LM7805 Positive Voltage Regulator
max_ratings: Absolute Max Input: 35V | Internal Thermal Overload & Short Circuit Protection
typical_applications: 5V power rails for microcontrollers and sensors
On-card regulation to eliminate distribution noise
critical_warnings: Linear dropout: Requires at least 2.0V headroom (Vin >= 7.0V for stable 5V output).
Power dissipation: Linear loss P = (Vin - 5V) * Iout. At 12V in and 500mA out, dissipates 3.5 Watts of heat — will overheat and shut down without a heatsink!
Requires 0.33µF input capacitor and 0.1µF output capacitor placed close to pins to prevent high-frequency oscillation.

name: ESP32-WROOM-32D Development Board
max_ratings: Absolute Max VDD: 3.6V | GPIO Max Voltage: 3.6V (NOT 5V tolerant)
peak_current: Up to 500mA during WiFi/BT RF transmit bursts
pin_configuration: EN (CHIP_PU): Reset / Enable (pull HIGH with 10k to run)
GPIO0: Boot mode selection (LOW for flashing)
GPIO2: Strapping pin (must be floating or LOW to boot)
key_features: Dual-core Xtensa 32-bit LX6 microprocessor up to 240 MHz
Integrated 802.11 b/g/n Wi-Fi and Bluetooth v4.2 BR/EDR and BLE
520 KB SRAM, 448 KB ROM, 4MB / 8MB SPI Flash
Capacitive touch, ADC, DAC, PWM, I2C, SPI, UART, CAN
critical_warnings: CRITICAL: GPIO pins are NOT 5V tolerant. Connecting 5V logic (e.g. 5V Arduino Uno signals) directly to ESP32 pins will permanently damage the silicon.
WiFi transmission causes sharp current spikes of ~500mA. Inadequate power supply or long wires cause brownout resets (Brownout detector was triggered).

name: 1N4007 Standard Recovery Rectifier Diode
peak_current: 30A non-repetitive peak forward surge (8.3ms half sine)
pin_configuration: Anode: Connected to lower potential / positive in forward bias
Cathode: Marked by silver/white stripe band
key_features: Low reverse leakage current (5µA max at 25°C)
typical_applications: Reverse polarity protection for low-current circuits
Flyback suppression diode for slow-switching inductive relays
critical_warnings: Standard recovery diode (reverse recovery time Trr is not specified, typically > 2-5µs). NOT suitable for high-frequency PWM (> 1 kHz) motor flyback! Use fast recovery or Schottky diodes (1N5819, UF4007) for PWM circuits to prevent switching spikes.
source_reference: Vishay General Semiconductor 1N4001 thru 1N4007 Datasheet Doc 88503
